entries.source_title: Difference between subjects, objects and pronouns - Grammar Point
entries.note: Subject/object terminology, noun replacement and the shift to preverbal object position are already explicit and exercised.

entries.source_title: Using French Stress Pronouns in compound subjects and objects (unlike English)
entries.note: Joined-subject agreement was sufficient; added an explicit joined direct object without a preposition and a courtesy-order note.

entries.source_title: Using le/la/l'/les = it/him/her/them (French Direct Object Pronouns)
entries.note: The full direct-object series, noun gender/number, vowel elision and people/thing reference already have contextual transformations.

entries.source_title: Using lui/leur = him or her/them (French Indirect Object Pronouns)
entries.note: Lui/leur selection follows French verb construction, includes a female recipient and contrasts direct verbs and stressed personal complements.

entries.source_title: Position of French Object Pronouns - with simple tenses
entries.note: Preverbal placement in a simple tense is explicitly taught and assessed, with affirmative commands correctly separated.

entries.source_title: Position of French Object Pronouns - with infinitives
entries.note: Existing instruction identifies which verb owns the object, rather than moving every pronoun mechanically to the infinitive; affirmative and negative transformations assess it.

entries.source_title: Tout/tous/toute/toutes = Everything/all (of them)/whole/completely in French
entries.note: Agreement and all/everything distinctions were sound; added explicit compound-tense placement and an assessed contrast between group reference and adverbial intensity.

entries.source_title: Quelqu'un/Quelqu'un d'autre = Someone/Someone else (French Indefinite Pronouns)
entries.note: Someone/else forms were present; added the neutral question sense of English anyone and contrasted existence with unrestricted choice.

entries.source_title: Using [French stress pronouns] + même(s) to express "myself/yourself/etc" in French
entries.note: All stressed + meme forms, generic soi, singular polite vous and emphasis versus reflexivity already receive teaching and construction tasks.

entries.source_title: Moi/toi/lui/elle/soi/nous/vous/eux/elles - advanced usages (French Stress Pronouns)
entries.note: Prepositional and generic stressed forms were sufficient; comparative and restrictive que now have explicit contrasts and distinct assessment.

entries.source_title: Y = There (French Adverbial Pronouns)
entries.note: Location reference, chez + person as a place, infinitive/auxiliary placement and origin de versus destination are already distinguished; published bank-origin clarification retained.

entries.source_title: En with quantities = Of them (French Adverbial Pronouns)
entries.note: Numbers, retained un/une and personal quantities were sufficient; added retained un autre/une autre for replacements and additional copies.

entries.source_title: Autre chose/quelque chose d'autre = Something else (French Indefinite Pronouns)
entries.note: Both something-else forms were taught; added their anything-else reading in a neutral question without confusing it with indiscriminate choice.

entries.source_title: L'autre/Les autres = The other one(s) (French Indefinite Pronouns)
entries.note: Known alternatives versus remaining group members, singular/plural forms and independent reference are already taught and tested.

entries.source_title: Expressing quantities in French with quelques/plusieurs/de nombreux = A few/several/many
entries.note: A few/several/many and numerous gender agreement have direct teaching and tasks; quantity words are not treated as fixed numeric thresholds.

entries.source_title: Me becomes moi in affirmative commands in the imperative mood (L'Impératif) in French
entries.note: Affirmative moi, hyphens, negative me restoration and elision before en are already explained and assessed.

entries.source_title: Using object pronouns le/la/les vs lui/leur in affirmative commands in the imperative mood (L'Impératif) in French
entries.note: Direct versus recipient pronouns follow the French verb construction; affirmative postverbal placement and relevant spelling are exercised.

entries.source_title: Chacun/chacune/chaque = each one/each (French Indefinite Adjectives and Pronouns)
entries.note: Chaque/chacun and noun-group agreement were sound; added d'entre + stressed plural pronoun while keeping singular subject agreement.

entries.source_title: Position of French Object Pronouns - with compound tenses
entries.note: Existing examples and transformations put direct/indirect pronouns before auxiliaries and distinguish their agreement effects.

entries.source_title: Le/la même and Les mêmes = The same (French Indefinite Pronouns)
entries.note: Same-one agreement was sufficient; added explicit que as the comparison link with independent construction evidence.

entries.source_title: Le mien/le tien/le sien/etc = Mine/yours/his/hers/its (French Possessive Pronouns)
entries.note: Every singular-owner possessive form, retained article and agreement with the possessed object rather than owner gender are explicit.

entries.source_title: Le nôtre/le vôtre/le leur/etc = Ours/yours/theirs (French Possessive Pronouns)
entries.note: All group-owner possessives, polite vous, circumflex retention and article contractions already have complete teaching and tasks.

entries.source_title: N'importe qui = Anyone (French Indefinite Pronouns)
entries.note: Added existence versus free-choice questions; retained legitimate negative uses rather than adopting an affirmative-only ban.

references.purpose: Check free-choice semantics and explicit negative uses against the source's affirmative-only wording.

entries.source_title: N'importe quoi = Nonsense, anything (French Indefinite Pronouns)
entries.note: Unrestricted anything, evaluative nonsense and context-sensitive negatives are already distinguished and assessed.

entries.source_title: Which form of the conjugated verb to pick between nous/vous/ils/elles in cases with multiple subjects (French Subject Pronouns)
entries.note: Speaker/addressee/third-person hierarchy, feminine versus mixed groups and optional resumed subject pronouns already have clear examples and tasks.

entries.source_title: Conjugate semi-regular -oyer/-ayer/-uyer verbs in the present tense in French (Le Présent)
entries.note: Full y/i distribution, invariant nous/vous stems and both accepted -ayer spellings already have complete models and assessment.

entries.source_title: Using the infinitive form of verbs to express the English "-ING"
entries.note: Activity infinitives, conjugated main verbs and subject-matched reflexive infinitives are already explicitly distinguished.

entries.source_title: Conjugate ouvrir/découvrir and derivatives in the present tense in French (Le Présent)
entries.note: The ouvrir model was sound; added productive couvrir/reopening forms with accepted alternatives and independent transfer items.

entries.source_title: Conjugate offrir/souffrir in the present tense in French (Le Présent)
entries.note: Complete offrir and souffrir paradigms already contrast with finir and have contextual production items.

entries.source_title: Expressing necessity and obligation in French with "il faut"
entries.note: General necessity and prohibition were sound; added personal il me/te/lui/nous/vous/leur faut, unchanged impersonal agreement and noun versus formal infinitive register.

entries.source_title: Conjugate cueillir and derivatives in the present tense in French (Le Présent)
entries.note: Cueillir/accueillir/recueillir formation was sufficient; added the meaningful reflexive se recueillir distinction and a complete pronoun paradigm.

entries.source_title: Conjugate savoir in the present tense in French (Le Présent)
entries.note: All savoir persons, fact and skill complements and distinction from familiarity are already taught and exercised.

entries.source_title: Conjugate connaître/paraître and derivatives in the present tense in French (Le Présent)
entries.note: Connaître/paraître were complete; extended transfer to naître and legal-appearance forms while retaining accepted reformed spellings.

entries.source_title: Conjugate voir and derivatives in the present tense in French (Le Présent)
entries.note: Voir's i/y distribution was sufficient; added explicit fuir forms and productive sight-family extensions, with a subject-change task.

entries.source_title: Conjugate suivre/vivre and derivatives in the present tense in French (Le Présent)
entries.note: Complete vivre/suivre forms, derivative transfer and suis ambiguity already have contextual explanation and exercise evidence.

entries.source_title: Conjugate rire/sourire in the present tense in French (Le Présent)
entries.note: Both complete rire/sourire paradigms and nous/vous spellings already have original use examples and tasks.

entries.source_title: Conjugate servir and other -VIR verbs in the present tense in French (Le Présent)
entries.note: Added servir/se servir de and second-helping constructions; corrected the misleading comparison of stem-final v with the initial v in vivre.

entries.source_title: Conjugate recevoir and other -cevoir verbs in the present tense in French (Le Présent)
entries.note: Three stems and cedilla rules were complete; added the reflexive realisation construction with a complete paradigm and assessed pronoun placement.

entries.source_title: Conjugate verbs in -aindre/-eindre/-oindre in the present tense in French (Le Présent)
entries.note: All three -indre models were sound; added reflexive complaint versus direct pity and productive derivative examples.

entries.source_title: Conjugate conduire and other -uire verbs in the present tense in French (Le Présent)
entries.note: Conduire-type plural s, complete forms and representative derivatives are already explicit, with separate cuire/fuir spellings preventing blind extrapolation.

entries.source_title: Plus que/Moins que/Autant que = More than/Less than/As much as (Comparisons with Verbs in French)
entries.note: Verb-versus-adverb comparison was sound; added both positions around a verb's object and an action-versus-object-quantity contrast.

entries.source_title: Conjugate regular verbs in the imperative mood in French (L'Impératif)
entries.note: All three imperative persons, subject omission, -er versus other endings and relevant irregular sets are already explicit.

entries.source_title: Conjugate courir in the present tense in French (Le Présent)
entries.note: Complete courir forms, no -iss-, derivative transfer and present one-r versus future two-r spelling already have evidence.

entries.source_title: Conjugate regular -er verbs (+ avoir) in the compound past in French (Le Passé Composé)
entries.note: Auxiliary formation, every person, -er to -é and absence of subject agreement are already visible and exercised.

entries.source_title: Conjugate regular -ir verbs (+ avoir) in the compound past in French (Le Passé Composé)
entries.note: Regular finir-family participles were sound; added dormir/servir as -i participles despite their irregular presents.

entries.source_title: Using the French compound past (Le Passé Composé) to express sentences in the English simple past
entries.note: Completed events, two-part French versus simple English past and contextual present-perfect translations already have teaching and tasks.

entries.source_title: Conjugate regular -dre verbs (+ avoir) in the compound past in French (Le Passé Composé)
entries.note: Regular -dre formation and prendre contrast were sound; added coudre/cousu as a concrete exception to the tempting spelling shortcut.

entries.source_title: Conjugate dire (+avoir) in the compound past in French (Le Passé Composé)
entries.note: Dire/dit formation was sound; added derivative transfer with a genuine present-to-past transformation.

entries.source_title: Conjugate faire (+ avoir) in the compound past in French (Le Passé Composé)
entries.note: Fait with every avoir person and no subject agreement are already explicit and assessed in practical contexts.

entries.source_title: Conjugate avoir (+ avoir) in the compound past in French (Le Passé Composé)
entries.note: Auxiliary avoir versus participle eu is explicitly separated and tested for multiple persons.

entries.source_title: Conjugate être (+ avoir) in the compound past in French (Le Passé Composé)
entries.note: Être uses avoir + été; the lesson already contrasts auxiliary choice and adjective agreement without changing été.

entries.source_title: Conjugate coming and going verbs (+ être) in the compound past in French (Le Passé Composé)
entries.note: The selected coming/going inventory, auxiliary choice, complete agreement model and transitive switches are already taught.

entries.source_title: Agreeing past participle with subject's gender and number with (+ être) verbs in the compound past in French (Le Passé Composé)
entries.note: Gender/number agreement, mixed groups, singular polite vous and referential on are already explicit with constrained keys.

entries.source_title: Conjugate mourir, naître, décéder, devenir, rester (+ être) in the compound past in French (Le Passé Composé)
entries.note: Birth/death/becoming/staying participles, être auxiliaries and relevant agreement are all already taught and exercised.

entries.source_title: Conjugate reflexive verbs (+être) in the compound past in French (Le Passé Composé)
entries.note: Retained direct/indirect reflexive agreement analysis rather than the public body's unconditional subject-agreement wording.

references.purpose: Confirm agreement when se is direct, nonagreement with a following direct object, and invariable se parler.

entries.source_title: Conjugate prendre and derivatives (+avoir) in the compound past in French (Le Passé Composé)
entries.note: Pris-family formation was sufficient; added se méprendre to the later reflexive lesson so family resemblance does not imply avoir.

entries.source_title: Conjugate voir/devoir/pouvoir/boire/croire/savoir/lire/plaire/taire (+ avoir) in the compound past in French (Le Passé Composé)
entries.note: Every named short -u participle, the accent in dû, auxiliary model and distinct meanings already have direct evidence.

entries.source_title: Conjugate mettre and derivatives (+avoir) in the compound past in French (Le Passé Composé)
entries.note: Mis and productive mettre derivatives already have an explicit transfer model, final-s explanation and independent items.

entries.source_title: Conjugate ouvrir/découvrir and derivatives (+ avoir) in the compound past in French (Le Passé Composé)
entries.note: Ouvert/découvert/recouvert already demonstrate the irregular -vert family rather than applying present -er-like endings to the participle.

entries.source_title: Conjugate recevoir and other -cevoir verbs (+avoir) in the compound past in French (Le Passé Composé)
entries.note: -Çu participles and cedilla were sufficient; added the auxiliary-changing s'apercevoir construction to the later reflexive lesson.

entries.source_title: Conjugate -aindre, -eindre, -oindre verbs (+ avoir) in the compound past in French (Le Passé Composé)
entries.note: -Aint/-eint/-oint formation was sound; added the pronominal complaint exception to auxiliary choice in the later reflexive lesson.

entries.source_title: Conjugate regular verbs in the imperfect tense in French (L'Imparfait)
entries.note: Nous-stem derivation, all six endings, regular/irregular transfers and i/y before -ions are already visible and assessed.

entries.source_title: Expressing continuing action with the imperfect tense in French (L'Imparfait)
entries.note: Ongoing past viewpoint versus completed events already has paired examples and a constrained activity-in-progress task.

entries.source_title: Using the compound tense (Le Passé Composé) on its own or with the imperfect tense (L'Imparfait)
entries.note: Event sequences without obligatory background, interrupted activity, long bounded intervals and viewpoint differences already have meaningful contrasts.

entries.source_title: Conjugate être in the imperfect tense in French (L'Imparfait)
entries.note: Exceptional ét- stem and all être imperfect forms are complete, with multiple persons tested.

entries.source_title: Expressing opinions and describing with the imperfect tense in French (L'Imparfait)
entries.note: Past descriptions and opinions are already explained as viewpoints, including a useful contrast with bounded reactions.

entries.source_title: Conjugate semi-regular -cer verbs in the imperfect tense in French (L'Imparfait)
entries.note: Sound-preserving ç before a and plain c before i are explicitly explained in a complete paradigm and varied tasks.

entries.source_title: Conjugate semi-regular -ger verbs in the imperfect tense in French (L'Imparfait)
entries.note: The -ger e before a versus omission before i is explained through sound and assessed beyond one verb.

entries.source_title: Expressing past habits or repeated actions with the imperfect tense in French (L'Imparfait)
entries.note: Open past habits and counted completed repetitions are already separated; learners are not taught that repetition mechanically dictates tense.

entries.source_title: Conjugate reflexive verbs in the imperfect tense in French (L'Imparfait)
entries.note: Reflexive pronouns, complete imperfect forms and no auxiliary are already explicit; vowel elision is established in the prerequisite reflexive lesson.

entries.source_title: Conjugate conduire and other -uire verbs in the compound past in French (Le Passé Composé)
entries.note: Conduit-family -uit formation, no inserted present-stem s and avoir despite movement are already taught and assessed.

entries.source_title: Conjugate tenir and derivatives (+avoir) in the French compound past (Le Passé Composé)
entries.note: Tenu-family transfer and contrast with venir's être auxiliary already have examples, complete auxiliary patterns and multiple derivatives assessed.

entries.source_title: Conjugate suivre (+avoir) in the compound past in French (Le Passé Composé)
entries.note: Suivi/poursuivi, auxiliary choice and course-taking versus following meanings already have concrete teaching and tasks.

entries.source_title: Conjugate écrire and derivatives (+avoir) in the compound past in French (Le Passé Composé)
entries.note: Écrit-family spelling was sufficient; added registration of oneself versus another person to make the reflexive auxiliary switch explicit.

entries.source_title: Conjugate offrir and souffrir (+ avoir) in the compound past in French (Le Passé Composé)
entries.note: Offert/souffert and avoir are already explicit, with the present-pattern trap and absence of subject agreement explained.

entries.source_title: Conjugate vivre (+avoir) in the compound past in French (Le Passé Composé)
entries.note: Vécu versus vu, avoir rather than être and vivre-family transfer are already taught with a relevant construction item.

entries.source_title: Conjugate vouloir (+avoir) in the compound past in French (Le Passé Composé)
entries.note: Voulu formation, specific intention/attempt, negation and lack of guaranteed success are already explicit and exercised.

entries.source_title: Monter dans, descendre de = To get on, off transportation in French (prepositions)
entries.note: Passenger entry versus exit, dans/de and article contraction are already taught; the physical-surface contrast prevents literal English transfer.

entries.source_title: Using the present tense (Le Présent) - and not the compound past (Le Passé Composé) - in sentences with "depuis" (since/for) in French (French Prepositions of Time)
entries.note: Continuing present plus depuis, elapsed duration versus starting point and completed events within a since-period are already separated without a blanket tense ban.

entries.source_title: After/before versus in front of/behind (French Prepositions of Time and Place)
entries.note: Time/space distinction was sound; added the queue case where physical position and service order can both be described.

entries.source_title: Expressing for + [duration] in French with either pendant/durant/depuis/pour (French Prepositions of Time)
entries.note: Added omitted pendant and habitual bounded versus currently continuing intervals; retained planned pour duration when a booking is reported in the past, not a future-tense-only rule.

references.purpose: Check duration and intended temporal reference rather than infer a required grammatical tense from pour.

entries.source_title: En vs Dans with time (French Prepositions of Time)
entries.note: Completion time versus future delay was sound; added calendar month/year reference so en is not reduced to a duration marker.

entries.source_title: Aimer = to love, like something/someone in French
entries.note: Aimer/bien intensity was sound; added mild compound-past dislike and strong liking without equating it mechanically with romantic love.

references.purpose: Check contextual affection, friendship, love and adverb-modified liking; not used as evidence for a blanket negative-syntax prohibition.

entries.source_title: Expressing "to find" and opinions with the verb "trouver" in French
entries.note: Finding versus judging, mandatory clause link, adjective agreement and direct pronoun placement are already taught and tested.

entries.source_title: "Sentir bon" vs "Se sentir bien" - The different meanings of the verb "sentir" in French
entries.note: Sensing an object, invariant smell adjectives, reflexive well-being and agreeing state adjectives already have complete forms and contrastive tasks.

entries.source_title: Avoir raison/tort/de la chance = To be right/wrong/lucky (French Expressions with avoir)
entries.note: Avoir versus English be was sound; added negative luck with de rather than de la, including a compound-tense transformation.

entries.source_title: Expressing you like something/someone in French with the verb "plaire"
entries.note: Thing-as-subject plaire was sound; added personal appeal, reversed experiencer roles and making someone happy with faire plaisir.

entries.source_title: Aller à = to suit someone (French Expressions with aller)
entries.note: Clothing fit, suitability of an arrangement and indirect experiencer pronouns already have complete forms and contextual application.

entries.source_title: Visiter vs Rendre visite à whether you visit a place or a person
entries.note: Retained ordinary social rendre visite à without adopting the public body's universal ban on visiter a person.

references.purpose: Confirm direct-person uses, especially assisting or caring for a patient or prisoner.

entries.source_title: Connaître vs savoir = to know something vs to know how to do in French
entries.note: Familiarity, facts, embedded questions and infinitive skills are already separated; noun complements of savoir are not wrongly prohibited.

entries.source_title: Expressing "to walk" with se promener/promener/marcher/aller à pied in French
entries.note: Walking activity, transport, strolling and taking another being out already have distinct examples, complete promener forms and tasks.

entries.source_title: Using manquer (à) to say you miss someone or something emotionally in French
entries.note: Missed entity versus experiencer, indirect pronouns, plural subject agreement and unchanged roles in the past already have explicit transformations.

entries.source_title: Using manquer (de) to say you/something miss or lack in French
entries.note: Missed events and general lack were sound; added impersonal personal shortfalls and why their determiner differs from manquer de.

entries.source_title: Avoir honte de = to be ashamed of (French Expressions with avoir)
entries.note: Honte de nouns/infinitives was sound; added stressed-person complements and a construction contrast with preverbal indirect pronouns.

entries.source_title: Faire exprès (de) = To do something on purpose (French Expressions with faire)
entries.note: Intentional action, de plus infinitive, past formation and denial of intent rather than denial of the event are already explicit.

entries.source_title: Faire mal à vs Faire du mal à = to hurt someone (French Expressions with faire)
entries.note: Retained overlapping pain/harm meanings rather than an exclusive physical-versus-emotional split.

references.purpose: Check the broad harm meaning and both physical pain and figurative suffering under mal.

entries.source_title: Il y a + [durée] = [duration] + ago (French Expressions of Time)
entries.note: Il y a before a duration already dates an event ago and is distinguished from interval length and existential il y a.

entries.source_title: Faire peur (à) = To scare someone (French Expressions with faire)
entries.note: The frightening entity controls faire and the affected person is indirect; article contraction and pronoun replacement already have evidence.

entries.source_title: Faire la queue = To queue/To be in line/To stand in line (French Expressions with faire)
entries.note: The fixed queue expression is taught as waiting rather than literal making, with complete faire forms and a regional file alternative.

entries.source_title: Expressing timeliness in French - late/early - precise
entries.note: Avoir/être amounts were sound; added event verbs with avec + duration + de retard and the alternative duration + en retard order.

entries.source_title: Se souvenir de/Se rappeler (de) = To remember something in French
entries.note: Retained the published formal/colloquial distinction and permitted de caveats; the source's broad interchangeability wording does not erase editing conventions.

references.purpose: Check noun, stressed-person, reminder-infinitive and noun-internal en constructions, not just the usual direct-object rule.

entries.source_title: Faire partie de = To be part of (French Expressions with faire)
entries.note: Partie spelling, de contraction and belonging rather than leaving already have teaching, examples and construction tasks.

entries.source_title: Expressing ongoing actions in the past in French: être en train de
entries.note: The baseline already allows both background opinions and bounded reactions; its viewpoint explanation is not an automatic verb-to-tense rule.

entries.source_title: Faire confiance (à) = To trust (French Expressions with faire)
entries.note: Confiance à was sound; added an explicit past indirect-pronoun transformation to distinguish it from stressed complements after de.

entries.source_title: Using "devoir" in the imperfect tense versus the compound past in French (L'Imparfait vs Le Passé Composé)
entries.note: Devoir already separates background obligation, bounded requirement and inference; completed action is not falsely guaranteed by tense alone.

entries.source_title: Avoir l'habitude de = To be in the habit of, to tend to (French Expressions with avoir)
entries.note: Habit and being accustomed to, required de, complete present forms and past imperfect contrast already have practical examples and tasks.

entries.source_title: Demi/moitié/etc = Half in French
entries.note: Demi- invariance and hyphen, et demie gender-only agreement, moitié de contraction and à moitié states already have direct assessment.

entries.source_title: S'en aller = To leave in French
entries.note: Public body read, but comparison of its postauxiliary en order remains unfinished. The accessible Robert and Usito passages did not settle that alternative, and full Larousse access returned HTTP 503. Existing standard-model evidence alone does not establish teaching-depth sufficiency; no unsupported register or correctness judgment is made.

references.purpose: Read the preauxiliary en departure example; it does not adjudicate the alternative order.
Read the departure and destination senses of s'en aller; these passages do not resolve the alternate compound order.

entries.source_title: Common mistakes with mon/ma/mes, ton/ta/tes and son/sa/ses (French Possessive Adjectives)
entries.note: All owner series and agreement with the possessed noun rather than owner gender already have explicit examples and fair constrained keys.

entries.source_title: "Ma" becomes "mon" with feminine nouns starting with a vowel or mute h (French Possessive Adjectives)
entries.note: Vowel nouns and intervening consonants were sound; added vowel-starting adjectives and consonantal initial y with a decision method.

entries.source_title: Bien, mal, mieux, moins, peu (Irregular French Adverbs)
entries.note: Core irregular meanings and gentil were sound; added bref/brièvement with a contextual transformation rather than an adjective-to-adverb meaning shortcut.

entries.source_title: Ce/cet/cette and ces = this/that and these/those (French Demonstrative Adjectives)
entries.note: All four demonstratives, masculine vowel/mute-h selection, feminine cette and contextual proximity are already explicit and assessed.

entries.source_title: Forming adverbs from adjectives ending in a vowel in French (French Adverbs)
entries.note: Vowel-ending formation, exceptions and genuine sentence transformations already exist; published aisément and élégamment items are retained.

entries.source_title: Position of French Adverbs - general rule
entries.note: Simple postverbal adverbs are already taught in a broader target-based method, without treating the short source's ordinary position as universal.

entries.source_title: Special cases when you use mon/ma/mes/etc with parts of the body (French Possessive Adjectives)
entries.note: Default body-part articles, independently described or emphasised possession and another person's involvement already have contextual teaching.

entries.source_title: Forming the feminine of adjectives ending in -f in French
entries.note: F-to-ve formation, plural agreement and bref's accent exception are already explicit in the complete adjective models.

entries.source_title: Plus ... que/Moins ... que/Aussi ... que = More ... than/Less ... than/As ... as (Comparisons with Adjectives in French)
entries.note: All three adjective comparisons, noun agreement and stressed comparison pronouns already have meaningful examples and construction tasks.

entries.source_title: Adjectives after personne, rien, tout le monde, quelqu'un are always masculine in French
entries.note: Generic masculine singular agreement and the feminine noun une personne contrast are already explicit; exercises constrain generic rather than identified-person readings.

references.purpose: Confirm the ordinary neutral-pronoun masculine singular agreement and singular verb.

entries.source_title: Forming adverbs from adjectives ending in -ant and -ent in French (French Adverbs)
entries.note: -Ant/-ent spelling and shared sound were sound; added couramment as a language-skill construction rather than applying courant to a fluent person.

entries.source_title: Plus ... que/Moins ... que/Aussi ... que = More ... than/Less ... than/As ... as (Comparisons with Adverbs in French)
entries.note: Adverb comparison and invariance, including stressed comparison pronouns, are already separated from adjective agreement and action amounts.

entries.source_title: D'autres vs des autres = others (French Indefinite Adjectives)
entries.note: Possessive des autres was sound; added an unspecified complement after a de-verb so learners do not overgeneralise that de automatically requires des autres.

entries.source_title: Forming the feminine of adjectives ending in -c in French
entries.note: All relevant -che/-que forms and grecque/sèche exceptions already have full models and contextual tasks without an absolute sound shortcut.

entries.source_title: Position of French Adverbs - with compound tenses
entries.note: Short adverbs between auxiliary and participle, longer manner adverbs and flexible time placement are already taught as tendencies with explicitly positioned tasks.

entries.source_title: Forming the feminine of adjectives ending in -oux + "faux" in French
entries.note: Douce, rousse, jalouse and fausse already have complete gender-number sets, spelling contrasts and distinct contextual assessment.

entries.source_title: De plus en plus / De moins en moins + [adverbe/adjectif/verbe] = more and more / less and less + [adverb/adjective/verb] (Comparisons in French)
entries.note: Increasing/decreasing adjectives, adverbs and actions are already contrasted with noun quantities; no unneeded final de is introduced.

entries.source_title: Frais, long, favori, rigolo have irregular feminine forms (French adjectives)
entries.note: All four irregular adjective sets, informal rigolo and accepted fraiche spelling already have teaching and relevant keys.

entries.source_title: Using son/sa/ses to express possession with personne/tout le monde/chacun/il faut (French Possessive Adjectives)
entries.note: Generic individual possessions use son/sa/ses with explicit agreement tasks; il faut is not treated as making a specifically addressed person's possessive impossible.

entries.source_title: Using notre/nos versus son/sa/ses with "on" depending on its meaning (French Possessive Adjectives)
entries.note: Generic on and identified-group on are already distinguished without banning each person's own possession in a conversational group.

entries.source_title: Quel/quelle/quels/quelles + [nom] = What a [noun] (French Exclamative Adjectives)
entries.note: Exclamative quel agreement, absence of an extra indefinite article and context versus interrogative use already have explicit tasks.

entries.source_title: Le plus/Le moins = The most/the least (Superlative with Adverbs in French)
entries.note: Adverb superlatives retain invariable le and the adverb spelling; ranking is already contrasted with an agreeing adjective superlative.

entries.source_title: Le plus/Le moins = The most/the least (Superlative with Verbs in French)
entries.note: Verb superlatives retain le and follow the action; both least and most are already assessed without subject-gender agreement.

entries.source_title: Ne ... pas du tout = Not at all (French Negations)
entries.note: Strong denial was sound; added separated du tout after an object while preserving ne/pas around the auxiliary.

entries.source_title: Ne ... plus = No more/no longer (French Negations)
entries.note: Ended situation versus not-yet expectation, placement and no extra pas already have contextual transformations; audio and pronunciation performance are outside the audit.

entries.source_title: Ne ... personne = No one/nobody (French Negations)
entries.note: Nobody versus une personne, retained prepositions and short replies already have explicit teaching and full-sentence practice.

entries.source_title: Ne ... rien = Nothing (French Negations)
entries.note: Nothing versus anything under negation and standalone replies already have examples and correctly positioned compound-tense transformations.

entries.source_title: Position of French Object Pronouns - with negations
entries.note: Complete public article confirms the preverbal negative pattern already taught; simple, compound and infinitive negative transformations supply evidence.

entries.source_title: N'avoir plus de = To have none left (French Negations)
entries.note: Exhausted quantities, de/d' and count-noun plurals already have contrasted examples and original sentence transformations.

entries.source_title: Using restrictive ne … que to express only with simple tenses (French Negations)
entries.note: Positive restriction, que's scope, vowel elision and retained positive articles already have teaching and meaningful alternatives.

entries.source_title: Ne ... pas non plus = Not ... either (French Negations)
entries.note: Adding a second negative was sound; added non plus after the object instead of implying it must stay adjacent to pas.

entries.source_title: Ne ... aucun(e) = None (French Negations)
entries.note: Gender, ordinary singular count nouns, direct noun attachment and absence of pas are already explicit; existing plural-only-noun caveat is retained.

entries.source_title: Ne ... pas assez (de) = Not enough (of) (French Negations)
entries.note: Insufficient action, adjective and noun quantity are already separated, with required de/d' only in the noun pattern.

entries.source_title: Ne ... ni ... ni = Neither ... nor (French Negations)
entries.note: Both exclusions, omitted unspecified articles and retained definite articles already have paired examples and transformations.

entries.source_title: Forming simple negative commands with the imperative mood in French (L'Impératif)
entries.note: Negative ne/pas placement and restoration of before-verb pronouns are already covered, including reflexive commands.

entries.source_title: Ne ... pas = Not - with compound tenses (French Negations)
entries.note: Ne/pas around avoir or être rather than the participle already has affirmative-to-negative transformations for both auxiliaries.

entries.source_title: Ne ... pas grand-chose = Not ... much (French Negations)
entries.note: Not much versus zero, fixed grand-chose hyphen and post-participle position already have examples and keys.

entries.source_title: Ne ... pas encore = Not yet (French Negations)
entries.note: Expected but incomplete actions and core contiguous pas encore before participles are already contrasted with no-longer actions.

entries.source_title: Quel/quels/quelle/quelles ? = Which/what? (French Question Words)
entries.note: Quel with nouns was sound; added all four lequel replacement forms and a known-options transformation.

entries.source_title: Inverted questions in the present tense (Le Présent) in French - regular forms (except il/elle/on forms)
entries.note: Subject-pronoun inversion, hyphens, question-word introduction and natural noninverted alternatives already have varied tasks.

entries.source_title: Que + [inverted statement] ? = What ... ? (French Questions)
entries.note: Que with pronoun inversion was sound; added a noun subject after the verb and explicit contrast with qu'est-ce que order.

entries.source_title: Inverted questions in the present tense (Le Présent) in French - il/elle/on forms
entries.note: Inserted -t- versus retained final t/d, il/elle/on and question-word uses already have clear sound/spelling explanation and assessment.

entries.source_title: Qui/Qui est-ce qui [conjugated verb] ? = Who ... ? (French Questions)
entries.note: Short and expanded subject-person questions, no extra subject pronoun and distinction from object qui are already explicit.

entries.source_title: Qui/Qui est-ce que ... ? = Whom ... ? (French Questions)
entries.note: All three person-object question patterns are already distinguished by construction and register, with no inversion after est-ce que.

entries.source_title: Inverted questions with reflexive verbs in the present tense (Le Présent) in French
entries.note: Reflexive-before-verb versus subject-after-verb roles and repeated noun subjects are already taught; transformations distinguish the two vous positions.

entries.source_title: Inverted questions in the compound past (Le Passé Composé) in French - with subject pronouns
entries.note: Only the auxiliary inverts; both auxiliaries and linking t already have direct examples and constructed past questions.

entries.source_title: Inverted questions in the present tense (Le Présent) in French - with names/things/emphasis
entries.note: Complex inversion preserves the noun and resumes it with an agreeing pronoun; present and compound examples already prevent a noun-swap shortcut.

entries.source_title: Inverted questions in the present tense (Le Présent) in French - special cases "puis-je/ai-je/suis-je"
entries.note: Puis-je/ai-je/suis-je were sound; added vais-je with movement and near-future infinitive chains.

entries.source_title: Qu'est-ce qui + [conjugated verb] = What [does]... (French Questions)
entries.note: Thing-subject questions were sound; added plaire's experiencer trap so English subject order does not misidentify French qui.

entries.source_title: Using "une dizaine" and other approximate numbers in French
entries.note: Approximate noun quantities were sound; added quinzaine/two-week estimates and dizaines without forcing multiples of twelve.

entries.source_title: Prochain/Dernier = Next/Last + [durations] in French
entries.note: Calendar adjective position was sound; added month/season frames and relative-day vocabulary, with seasonal construction assessment.

entries.source_title: Expressing intervals of dates and times in French = from ... to ...
entries.note: Dates, hours and recurring weekdays were sound; added one-off weekdays, month intervals and exact-hour omission.

entries.source_title: Doing arithmetic in French - addition, subtraction, multiplication, division
entries.note: All arithmetic operations were sound; added the singular verbal equality reading and distinguished égale from the sign label égal.

entries.source_title: Some plural English nouns are singular in French and vice versa
entries.note: Garments, hair and holidays were sound; added singular collective heads and France's usual plural restroom expression versus singular personal grooming.

entries.source_title: De plus en plus de / de moins en moins de + [nom] = more and more / less and less + [nouns] (Comparisons in French)
entries.note: Increasing/decreasing noun quantities, mandatory de and distinction from action/quality trends already have complete teaching and tasks.

entries.source_title: Forming the plural of French nouns ending in -ou
entries.note: All seven -oux exceptions, regular -s contrasts, masculine headwords and meanings already have original examples and assessment; source mnemonics are not reused.

entries.source_title: Some French nouns have different meanings depending on whether they're masculine or feminine
entries.note: All gender-changing pairs in the public teaching body already have article/meaning contrasts and tasks, plus additional useful pairs; linked vocabulary expansions were not audited.
